**1. Shift focus outward.**  
Instead of worrying about how you come across, get curious about other people. Ask open-ended questions and listen actively — people feel valued when they’re heard.

**2. Find common ground quickly.**  
Bring up general topics most can relate to: food, local events, music, or hobbies. If you share a personal interest, invite others to contribute their own.

**3. Prepare a few conversation starters.**  
Having two or three ready-made questions or anecdotes makes the first moments smoother (“I heard this area has great street food — do you have a favorite spot?”).

**4. Use confident body language.**  
Eye contact, a relaxed posture, and open gestures can signal approachability even before you speak.

**5. Join in small group activities.**  
Collaborating on a casual game, project, or shared task can remove the pressure from one-on-one conversation and allow trust to grow naturally.

**6. Manage self-talk.**  
Replace “I don’t belong” thoughts with “I’m here to learn about others” — this reframes unfamiliarity as opportunity.
